language.note: Irish is the constitutional first official language, though English is the everyday majority language; bilingual road signage (Irish above English) is a strong, consistent visual identifier

terrainDescription.zh: 以綠色丘陵牧草地為主的溫帶海洋性氣候地形，中部多低地牧場，沿海地區地形起伏較大
terrainDescription.en: Temperate oceanic terrain dominated by green pastoral lowlands, with a low-lying central plain and more rugged coastal areas

plate.color: white background, black text; blue EU strip with 12 gold stars + "IRL" on the left; optional green strip on the right for zero-emission vehicles (since July 2025)

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Green-and-white bollards are a fairly reliable clue distinguishing Ireland from the UK

utilityPole.transformerMount: Wooden poles, occasionally with metal crossbars (similar to the UK); yellow electrical-hazard stickers show only a lightning bolt with no human figure (unlike the UK's), often paired with a second black-outlined rectangular sticker below — a subtle but useful UK/Ireland differentiator

historicalContext.zh: 愛爾蘭雖與英國同樣靠左行駛，卻已於2005年改用公制公里標示距離，且警告標誌採用美式黃色菱形（而非英國/歐陸常見的紅框三角形），是歐洲道路標誌中相當獨特的混合案例。
historicalContext.en: Despite driving on the left like the UK, Ireland switched to metric kilometers for road distances in 2005, and its warning signs use American-style yellow diamonds rather than the red-bordered triangles common in the UK and continental Europe — a genuinely unusual hybrid case in Europe.
